sections.heading: One Company for Every Trade
body: A remodel is never one job. It's carpentry, plumbing, wiring, tile and paint, and each one has to finish before the next can start.
Hire them separately and you become the project manager. You're the one calling the tile setter because the plumber ran late, or finding out the electrician was never told the wall moved.
We run every one of those trades ourselves. Our crews are licensed and insured in carpentry, tile and flooring, plumbing, electrical and painting, so you make one call and get one plan.
It also makes the next project easier. The crew that already knows your house is the crew that does your next room.

sections.heading: Bathroom Remodeling
body: Most people call us about a bathroom for the same few reasons. The shower is a builder-grade box that's been there for decades, the grout keeps cracking, or a leak showed up in the ceiling below.
Almost every shower problem is a water problem. Tile looks waterproof, but what keeps water out of your walls and floor is what sits behind the tile.
That's where I started. I began as a tile installer, so I know where showers fail.
We build walk-in showers, tile walls and floors, and make vanities to fit the room.
A designer on our own team works with you one-on-one on the layout and the materials.

sections.quote: We had a relatively small-scale master bathroom walk-in shower remodel, and the team treated us, and our home, like royalty. … From working one-on-one with their in house designer, to the tradesmen, to the owners themselves, we had nothing but a smooth and pleasant remodel experience.
sections.name: Amy B.

sections.heading: Kitchen Remodeling
body: A kitchen that doesn't work usually isn't one bad thing. It's worn flooring, cabinets that don't hold what you own, counters with nowhere to set a hot pan, and a layout that makes two people trip over each other.
Those pieces all meet in the same room, so they're best planned together. Move a sink and the plumbing, the cabinets and the floor all change with it.
We do the floors, cabinets, counters and layout as one project, with one crew and one schedule. If the best fix is to rearrange the room, we'll show you how.

sections.heading: The Rest of the House
body: Bathrooms and kitchens are our main work, but they're not our only work. Every other room gets the same licensed crews and the same free estimate.
list: **Living space remodeling.** Whole rooms redone with new flooring, trim and paint.
**Custom cabinetry and woodworking.** Built-ins, shelving and cabinets made to fit the room, instead of a stock size with filler strips.
**Custom spaces.** An office, a laundry room or any room that needs its own plan, designed around how you use it.
**Outdoor living.** Decks and outdoor spaces, built by the crew that remodels your kitchen.
**In-house interior design.** A designer on our team to help with layouts, finishes and materials on any of the above.

sections.heading: Choosing Materials Without Stalling the Job
body: Tile, counters and cabinets are the part of a remodel that ends up on the calendar. When a material arrives late, the crew waits and the room sits torn up.

So we help you choose early and get everything ordered before the work starts. If you've already found the tile or fixtures you want somewhere else, bring them in. They're your bathroom and your kitchen.

sections.heading: Additions
body: When a house has run out of room, an addition has to line up with what's already there: floors that meet, a roofline that makes sense, plumbing and wiring tied in correctly.
That's easier when the same company does the old rooms and the new one. We add bedrooms, bathrooms and living space to the house you have.

sections.quote: Have used 3 times now, once to tile a room, once to remodel a master bedroom and bathroom, and one time to build an additional bathroom, bedroom and living area. Their work is absolutely incredible, their vision and their ability to transform my vision into actuality is beyond comparison. I’ll never use anyone else. Ever.

sections.heading: A Clean House at the End of Every Day
body: Remodeling is dusty, and the dust goes where the work isn't. Strangers walking through your house all day is the other part people dread.
We cover your floors and close off the work area with plastic. We use a vacuum system to hold down drywall and plaster dust.
You'll know when the crew is coming and when they're leaving, and we clean up at the end of each day and again when the project wraps.

sections.quote: His employees and/or sub contractors upon entering our house laid down paper to protect our floors and put up plastic to isolate the area and a vaccum system to control sheetrock/plaster dust. Geremy and the whole crew were respectful of our home; showed up as promised; let us know when they were leaving at the end of their day; cleaned up after each day and at the completion of the project and did a wonderful job.

sections.heading: Why a Shower Fails
body: A shower rarely fails where you can see it. Grout cracks, caulk peels and a tile comes loose, but those are signs, not the cause.
The cause is water getting behind the tile. Tile and grout don't make a shower waterproof. A membrane or liner behind them does, and so does the way the floor of the shower is sloped and sealed.
When that layer is wrong, water soaks the wall and the floor underneath for years. The first sign can be a stain on the ceiling below.
That's why the first question to ask any contractor is how they'll waterproof your shower.

No cracking grout, no uneven floor tiles, no peeling shower caulk, no cracking walls, on and on.

sections.heading: Showers and Tile
body: I began my career setting tile, so tile is where I look first. A good tile job is level and plumb, the lines meet where they should, and the grout holds up after years of steam and cleaning.
We build walk-in showers, and we tile walls and floors. Swapping a builder-grade shower for a walk-in is one of the most common bathroom projects.

Our crews are licensed and insured in tile and flooring, plumbing, carpentry, electrical and painting. So the person who moves the drain is on the same team as the person who sets the tile on top of it.
A bathroom remodel is more than the shower. New lighting, outlets, a mirror, towel bars and fresh paint finish the room, and electrical and painting are two more of our own trades.
That keeps the end of the job from stalling. Nobody is waiting on a different contractor to hang a light or paint the wall.

sections.heading: When the Walls Come Open
body: Bathrooms hide their problems. A leak that has run for years looks fine until the old tile comes out.
If that happens in your bathroom, the job doesn't stop while you find a carpenter. Carpentry is one of our own trades, so rotted framing and floor get repaired as part of the same project.

We make custom vanities for the room. Each one is built for the room it goes in and matched to the rest of the bathroom.
We'll also work with what you already own. If there's a piece of furniture you love, we can look at turning it into the vanity.

items.q: How will you waterproof my shower?
items.a: Ask it of every contractor you talk to, us included, and get the answer before you sign anything. A contractor who says he'll figure it out later isn't ready to build your shower.

items.q: What if you find damage once the old shower is out?
items.a: It happens in older bathrooms. Because carpentry and plumbing are our own trades, we repair the framing and floor in the same project.

items.q: Can I buy my own tile or fixtures?
items.a: Yes. Choose with us, or bring what you've found. We've let homeowners source their own material when the supply house didn't have exactly what they wanted.

items.q: Do you only do full bathrooms?
items.a: No. We've done a walk-in shower on its own, a master bath and a guest bath. Tell us what you're replacing and we'll price that.

sections.heading: A Kitchen That Works Against You
body: You know the kitchen that fights you. The floor is worn through at the sink, the cabinets can't hold what you own, the counters are chipped or stained, and two people can't cook at once.
Sometimes new finishes fix it. Often the real problem is the layout: the sink is too far from the stove, the fridge door blocks the walkway, or a wall closes the room off from the rest of the house.
We'll tell you which one you have before you spend money on the wrong fix.

image.alt: Kitchen with wood cabinets, a tile backsplash and a stone countertop
image.brief: kitchen with wood cabinets, tile backsplash and stone countertop, cabinets on the right, window and plain wall on the left, no readable text, no people

sections.quote: Geremy and crew completely remodeled my kitchen, new floor, new cabinets, new counter tops, new appliances, and rearranged my kitchen floor plan. They did an awesome job. Every part of the work was done perfectly.
sections.name: Detha K.

sections.heading: Why a Kitchen Is Planned as One Project
body: Floor, cabinets, counters, plumbing and wiring all meet in the same room, and each one depends on the others. Cabinets can't be set until the floor and walls are ready.
Counters can't be measured until the cabinets are in. The sink and the stove need their plumbing and power where the new layout puts them.
Change the order and something gets torn out twice.
We run carpentry, flooring, plumbing, electrical, tile and paint ourselves, so the schedule is one schedule. Nobody waits on a different company to show up before the next step can start.

sections.heading: What Goes Into a Kitchen Remodel
body: A full kitchen remodel replaces the floor, the cabinets, the counters and often the sink and faucet, then finishes with tile backsplash, trim and paint. If the layout changes, the plumbing and wiring change with it.
Because those are all trades we run, the work isn't split between a kitchen company and a separate company for each trade.
A good layout starts with how you cook. Where you prep, where the trash goes and who walks through the room while you're at the stove decide where things belong, more than any catalog does.

sections.heading: Choosing Counters, Cabinets and Tile
body: Most of what makes a kitchen take longer than planned is material that isn't ready. Cabinets and stone are ordered to your measurements, and a late delivery leaves the room empty.
We help you choose early and get everything ordered before the work begins. Counters can be granite, stone or quartz, and we tile backsplashes to match.
Custom cabinetry and woodworking is one of our services too, so a kitchen can have cabinets made to fit an odd wall instead of a stock size that almost fits.

sections.quote: Geremy was also helpful at the beginning when we were picking the granite, stone and other materials we wanted. He gave us great guidance and had everything ordered so there were no delays.
sections.name: Carol W.

sections.heading: Floors, Trim and Paint
body: A new kitchen next to a tired hallway looks worse than the old one did. When the room is open anyway, it's the easiest time to carry new flooring, trim and paint past the kitchen door.
We do that work too. People have hired us for a kitchen and then had us redo most of the floor above it.

sections.heading: Your House While We Work
body: The kitchen is where you eat, and you'll be without it for part of the project. Dust and strangers in the house all day are the other part.

We cover your floors, remove the covers and vacuum when the day is done, and you know who's coming and when. A small table in another room, a coffee maker and a microwave get most families through it.

sections.quote: FHT did a full re-model on our kitchen and their work is incredible. From their “in house staff” to the contractors working in their name, The Farha team did an outstanding job for us.

Your customers already make your case: 25 of your 26 Google reviews are five stars, and they call the craftsmanship "top notch" and say your crew "cleaned up after each day". But your number sits at the bottom of every page in plain type, so someone on a phone has to copy it or call the next remodeler.

strategy.cardsHeading: Be the Home Remodeling Company People Find on Google
strategy.cardsIntro: Each card is one demo page: what costs you calls, and the fix.

cards.title: Homepage
cards.why: The page Google reads to learn what you do, and the first one people see.
problems: Your number sits at the very bottom as plain text. Nothing at the top lets someone tap to call.
The top of the page is a big logo with no photo of finished work, so visitors can't see what you build.
The headline is a slogan, "Wichita's Trusted Home Remodeling Contractors", and "trusted" is a claim nothing on the page backs up.
fixes: Your number is one tap to call on every page.
A photo of a finished kitchen at the top.
A headline that says home remodeling company in Wichita, KS, right at the top.
cards.alsoAdd: On day one, we sit down with you to get what makes you the obvious choice, every service you offer and every town you work in. That becomes the prescription: how many pages, in how many towns, so Google and AI tools can find you for every service.

cards.title: Bathroom Remodeling
cards.why: Showers and tile run through your reviews, yet this page is a photo gallery.
problems: The page address says "gallery", and under two short paragraphs it is mostly photos.
Nothing says how you waterproof a shower, the question one reviewer used to screen contractors.
fixes: A page for bathroom remodeling in Wichita, KS, with the address to match.
Showers, tile and vanities explained, with reviews beside each.
cards.alsoAdd: Pages planned from what Google actually shows for each search, so every page targets something people really look for.

cards.title: Kitchen Remodeling
cards.why: Kitchens are your other big room, with the same gallery setup.
problems: The page opens with brand names, then photos. It never says you do floors, counters and layouts.
fixes: A full page for kitchen remodeling in Wichita, KS.
Cabinets, counters, floors and layouts, with reviews beside each.
cards.alsoAdd: A check of what your competitors offer, so services you didn't think to mention still get their own pages.

cards.title: Contact
cards.why: The page where interest turns into a call.
problems: The menu on a phone has four items and no Contact link. The way in is a small "Request a Consultation!" line above the logo.
fixes: Your number in the menu bar on every page, one tap away.
A plain contact page with hours and what to have ready.
cards.alsoAdd: Call and form tracking that shows which pages and towns your leads come from.

closing.heading: Want a website like this for your business?
closing.text: Your customers call your work "top notch" and say you have "touched every room in the house". Book a strategy call with Fluid Frame to walk through this demo and confirm your full list of services.

onboardingQuestions: Geremy's surname is Farha on the site and in reviews; confirm how he wants to be introduced and who else to name (for example Kristen on the office side).
Phone: (316) 680-7514 is on the Google profile and the site. Confirm it is the number to lead with, and whether there is a second line.
Address: Google and the site show 1300 E Central Ave. Expertise.com and MapQuest list 1004 E 2nd St N, with MapQuest showing Closed. Which is current?
Hours: the contact page says Monday to Friday, 8 AM to 5 PM and closed weekends. Confirm they are current and match Google.
Years: the site says more than 20 years on the home and About pages and over 25 on the Our Staff page. Which do they want to say?

Brand and trade-group credentials named on the current site (Our Services, the kitchen page and the About page; full list in questions.md): ask for certificates or locator pages before we use any of them.
Licensing: the About page says crews are licensed and insured in five trades. Which license numbers and insurer can we show?
Service towns beyond Wichita: none are listed anywhere. Do they work in Derby, Andover, Maize or elsewhere?

Services to confirm: living spaces, outdoor and decks, custom spaces, additions, custom cabinetry, flooring, exterior doors, and whether they want flooring or decks on their own pages in a full build.
Shower waterproofing: which method does Geremy use, and does he want it named on the bathroom page?
Warranty and financing: a review mentions warranty work, but no terms are published. Is there a written warranty, and is financing offered?
Process: how an estimate visit works, typical project lengths, and who the day-to-day contact is, so the job steps on the service pages can be firmed up.
Logo files and brand colors (the demo uses placeholders until we have the real logo).
